Because most languages store decimal numbers in binary floating-point (IEEE 754 double precision). Just as 1/3 cannot be written exactly in decimal (0.333...), 0.1 and 0.2 cannot be represented exactly in base 2. Their stored values are slightly off: 0.1 is really about 0.1000000000000000055511, and 0.2 about 0.2000000000000000111022. When added, the rounding errors combine and the nearest representable result is about 0.30000000000000004, which is not the same as the nearest representable value of 0.3.

Use tolerance comparisons (e.g., `abs(a - b) < 1e-9`) or decimal types for exact decimal arithmetic.
